chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, who said:

I wrote to him, 'May I be your ransom,' 'It has been narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the patient who is unconscious for days: some said he must make up the prayer of the day on which he regains consciousness, and some said he must make up the prayer of three days and leave the rest, and some said there is no making up required of him.' So he wrote, 'He must make up the prayer of the day on which he regains consciousness.'
The correct view in these narrations is what we previously mentioned, that it is recommended (not obligatory).

key_terms.يَقْضِي: make up / perform the missed prayer
key_terms.يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: unconscious / in a state of swoon

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up prayers after a period of unconsciousness due to illness?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s resolution to the juristic debate regarding a patient who regains consciousness after days of unconsciousness, ruling that only the prayers of the specific day of awakening are made up. This ruling is contextualized within the broader Shia legal principle of *istihbab* (recommendation) rather than strict *wujub* (obligation), reflecting the Imam’s nuanced approach to easing burdens during illness. The text highlights the methodological importance of reconciling differing reports (*ikhtilaf*) through authoritative clarification (*takhrij*).
